The Advancing Front Framework is an isosurface extraction method that constructs a triangulated mesh by growing a front across the implicit surface, starting from a seed point and extending it edge-by-edge [S1].

The claim accurately reflects the information provided in Source [S1]. The source explicitly defines the Advancing Front Framework as an algorithm that 'begins with a seed point, and grow the triangulation across the surface' (matching 'starting from a seed point and extending it edge-by-edge'). It also confirms that the front is the 'boundary of the mesh' and is advanced by 'choosing an edge in the front and creating a new triangle attached to it' (matching 'constructs a triangulated mesh by growing a front'). Furthermore, the source identifies the method as being used for 'implicit surface triangulation' and operating on surfaces defined as 'isosurface[s]', which supports the classification as an 'isosurface extraction method'.

This directly supports the claim that front interference (self-intersection or intersection with other fronts) requires splitting or merging logic.
